findings.title: Kinship claim under sovereignty
findings.claim: The focus plainly alleges that the audience is given sons while female angels are taken for God; the pericope makes this a claim about divisible sovereignty as well as kinship. The supposed divine parties appear in a counterfactual as seekers of the throne, God is declared above what they say, and those invoked lack control and seek their own Lord.
findings.mechanism: The focus's selection verb and its opposed sons/female categories carry the allocation. The throne and transcendence in 17:42-43, followed by divine knowledge, genuine prophetic favor, denied agency, and seekers of nearness in 17:55-57, contact that allocation with a context where authority and approach remain with God.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the utterance is called grave: it distributes kinship as though sovereignty itself could be divided, while the surrounding passage keeps every alleged intermediary within dependence.
findings.containment: The direct claim about sons and female angels remains intact. This does not condemn every form of divine preference: 17:55 affirms differentiated prophetic favor. The reserved-share branch is a structural analogy, not a literal property or lexical translation, and the contextual links do not establish the historical referent of the claim.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel evidence names the allocation and its local carriers; the pericope contacts ground the sovereignty relation. The reserved-share facet is explicitly analogical.

findings.title: Speech beside unreceived praise
findings.claim: The focus's false-attribution branch can be read within a blocked-reception pattern: created praise is not grasped, repeated Quranic presentation increases aversion, and mention of the Lord alone is met with turning away. This makes the gendered attribution legible as a human account voiced alongside praise that its hearers do not understand.
findings.mechanism: The focus's qawl supplies the public assertion. At 17:44, universal tasbih meets an explicit failure to understand; 17:41 already says varied recitation intended for reminder increases flight, and 17:46 gives covered hearts, weighted hearing, and turning away when the Lord is named alone. Those contacts change the focus from a standalone false proposition to speech inside an account of failed reception.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees how a human social grammar can persist beside signs and praise that the passage says its audience does not receive.
findings.containment: The focus remains a claim about sons and female angels. The packet supports blockage and aversion, but the idea that familiar gender hierarchy fills an interpretive vacancy is an attributed inference, not a proven cause; simple juxtaposition remains possible.

epistemic.reason: The HFT source is legacy-unbound; the context roots and coordinates match the packet, while the replacement/projection mechanism remains an interpretation.

These relations change the focus from a general rejection of preference into a challenge to projecting self-benefiting kinship and agency onto God.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the pericope preserves differentiated favor while directing attention to who knows, who can act, and who remains dependent.
findings.containment: 17:55 may answer a different question from the focus, and 17:56-57 may address a distinct set of invoked beings; their relation to the selection verb remains a contextual audit, not proof that every distinction is endorsed or that the focus refers to a specific historical group.

epistemic.reason: The supplied ayat and all attributed roots/indices agree; the contrast that disciplines the focus selection is a pericope-level inference.

findings.title: Resistance that grows
findings.claim: The focus's grave saying can be read as one point in a wider response pattern: 17:59 pairs prior denial with warning signs, and 17:60 says a test and warning are followed by increased transgression. The pericope thus leaves open a feedback reading in which resistance grows under correction.

The explicit increase in 17:60 supplies an amplification link, changing the focus from a completed verbal offense into a possible stage in an escalating response.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the pericope's account of resistance as a process with consequences, while the focus remains a grave utterance.
findings.containment: The text does not explicitly identify the exact focus saying as the specific warning sign or prove that the listed outcomes form one causal loop. Parallel outcomes remain a live alternative; this is a qualified macro reading.

epistemic.reason: The candidate itself marks the metaphor exploratory; two branch records are supplied, while the interior-magnification branch and the load-bearing contact remain attributed.

findings.title: Prayer and a path of favor
findings.claim: As an external overlay, Fātiḥa 1:5-7 adds a specific first-person relation alongside the focus's allegation: worship and help are addressed to God alone, and guidance is requested toward the path of those God has favored.
findings.mechanism: The focus's public saying and preferential-selection carriers meet the external prayer's exclusive address in 1:5 and its request for guidance/path and bestowed favor in 1:6-7. The contact makes divine favor perceptible as a path people ask to follow, alongside the focus's assigned family categories.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader gains a concrete devotional act and a path-shaped account of favor, beyond the native pericope's diagnosis of unsupported allocation and intermediaries.
findings.containment: This is a contrast across the individually supplied ayat, not evidence that Fātiḥa directly answers 17:40. The native context already affirms differentiated favor and limits intermediary agency; the overlay adds the first-person worship/help formula and requested path without replacing the focus reading.

epistemic.reason: The external wording and root-occurrence coordinates are supplied exactly; the contact with the focus is a bounded interpretive overlay, not a documented allusion.
